html:
Cândido Rondon was a Brazilian army officer who built telegraph lines across the far west of Brazil and became the leading defender of its Indigenous peoples. The state of Rondônia is named after him.

Born in Mato Grosso, partly of Bororo and Terena descent, he led army commissions from the 1890s that strung telegraph lines through the wilderness, mapping huge areas. From 1907 the line toward the Madeira crossed the lands of the Paresi, Nambikwara and Aikanã. In 1914 he guided Theodore Roosevelt down the River of Doubt.

His motto was "die if necessary, but never kill". In 1910 he became the first head of the Indian Protection Service, which made peace with groups such as the Kaingang. Contact still brought epidemics, but his ideas shaped Brazilian policy, and he backed the Xingu park created in 1961.
sum: Cândido Rondon was a Brazilian army officer who built telegraph lines across the far west of Brazil and became the leading defender of its Indigenous peoples. The state of Rondônia is named after him.
